Bad service
Sep 2026 • Family
My family just had a meal at Son Bep Nha with a total of 6 adults, including my parents and my in-laws. Since this is a meeting between the two families, we chose the restaurant hoping for a comfortable, warm, and attentively served meal.

However, the actual experience was quite disappointing.

First, the wait time for the dish is too long. After ordering, my family had to wait almost 30 minutes before starting to receive the food. With a table full of elderly people, waiting that long is really uncomfortable. The white rice served was quite mushy. Although the staff member explained and offered to change the rice, my family declined because we didn't want to cause further trouble and wished to continue the meal in a cheerful atmosphere.

The issue that I find harder to accept lies in the tea service. When ordering, the staff advised that a teapot is only suitable for about two people. Because the table had six people, we proactively ordered two pots of tea as suggested by the restaurant.

During the meal, my mother felt the tea was quite strong and bitter, so she politely asked for more hot water to dilute it. However, the waiter replied that: "The restaurant only pours boiling water once, ma'am."

To be honest, this is the first time I've encountered such a regulation at a family restaurant. I have eaten at many restaurants in the same segment, and refilling hot water for tea is always a very normal thing. Especially when the guest is still using the tea pot they ordered and wishes to dilute the tea to suit their taste, limiting the number of times hot water can be poured creates a feeling of being too rigid and lacking in service sophistication.

What makes me dissatisfied is not the value of a boiling water bottle, but the customer experience. A little hot water is certainly not a significant cost for a restaurant, but the way it was refused made the customer feel like they were being nickel-and-dimed. For elderly people like our parents, flexibility and subtlety in service are sometimes more important than the food itself.

My family's total bill is over 2,300,000 VND and includes a 5% service charge. However, with what we experienced, I really did not feel the service quality was commensurate with this fee. Service fees are not just about bringing food to the table, but also reflect the level of care, manner of interaction, and ability to handle very basic customer needs.

Besides the points of dissatisfaction, I also want to give special praise to Tường Vi at the ground floor reception area. After my family finished eating, it started raining heavily. Vi proactively lent an umbrella to the family and even held an umbrella to shield my mother while she went to Takashimaya near the restaurant. You are very enthusiastic, polite, and especially show respect for elderly customers. This is a small action but leaves a very beautiful and worthy impression.

I hope the restaurant will review its service procedures, especially how they handle simple situations like providing extra hot water for guests drinking tea. These seemingly small things are actually the deciding factor for the customer experience and future return.
